### Summary

This 323-amino-acid protein is **EpmA**, the elongation factor P–(R)-β-lysine ligase, matching reviewed UniProt entry **A6VQ84** from *Actinobacillus succinogenes*. The sequence match is exact (100% identity and coverage), so the protein identification is strongly supported.

EpmA works with **EpmB** in the post-translational modification of **elongation factor P (EF-P)**. Its annotated role is to use ATP to activate (R)-β-lysine, then transfer it to a conserved lysine residue on EF-P. The reviewed reference annotates EpmA as a homodimer.

**Sequence characteristics:** predicted mass ~37.3 kDa; theoretical pI ~5.1; GRAVY −0.29, consistent with a mildly hydrophilic sequence. Pfam detects a tRNA-synt_2 family domain spanning residues 14–320. This domain annotation is consistent with the broader ligase family but does not by itself establish a tRNA-specific function.

These values are sequence-derived estimates. The homodimeric state and biochemical role come from the matched reference annotation, not direct experiments on a separately tested query protein.
